items.prompt: The exact factorization uses O(n^3) rational operations for n<=50. Which cost statement is accurate?

options.text: Every Fraction occupies one fixed-width machine word.
options.why: Fraction stores arbitrary-size integer numerator and denominator values.

options.text: Integer bit lengths and gcd costs also matter.
options.why: Counting rational operations does not prove constant cost per operation or a remote timing limit.

options.text: The operation count proves any external judge time limit is met.
options.why: A local bound is not an execution result against an unspecified service limit.

options.text: Exact arithmetic removes all memory growth.
options.why: The method stores O(n^2) fractions, whose integer representations also consume memory.

items.explanation: Counting rational operations does not prove constant cost per operation or a remote timing limit.
